Folate’s indirect constraint on BHMT remains unresolved.

Dietary protein provides digestible methionine, but this does not establish that increasing protein or methionine intake increases MAT-dependent SAMe synthesis in humans. DIAAS evaluates sulfur amino acids as methionine + cysteine.
Dietary protein supplies methionine. It does not show that eating more protein increases cycle rates. DIAAS scores sulfur amino acids as methionine plus cysteine.

Salvage of food vitamin B6 to pyridoxal 5'-phosphate does not show that higher vitamin B6 intake increases cystathionine beta-synthase or cystathionine gamma-lyase flux. Moderate B6 restriction changed cystathionine handling but did not significantly reduce total transsulfuration in the assessed human tracer study.

A formula that removed methionine and cysteine together slowed whole-blood synthesis, so that result does not isolate methionine. In the cysteine-free study, methionine intake stayed adequate and red-cell synthesis did not fall. This does not show that eating more methionine, once intake is adequate, raises glutathione synthesis.

The synthesis increase was measured in older adults given this precursor together with glycine. It does not show an effect of N-acetylcysteine alone, of ordinary foods, or of supplementation outside that group, and it is not a neuronal or clinical result.
Plasma tracing does not measure absolute hepatic flux, intermediary SAM, ordinary-food equivalence or benefit.
The review does not show that eating more riboflavin, once flavin mononucleotide (FMN) is adequate, raises electron transport. Riboflavin-responsive complex I disease is a separate clinical context.
Most cells outside the liver do not run the full route. The review does not establish what share of the NAD⁺ pool comes from tryptophan, and eating more protein is not shown to raise NAD⁺.

Production depends on fibre structure, dose and microbial ecology. Evidence for specific fibres must not be generalised to all fibre, and this relationship does not establish a universal intake threshold or response.
Conversion and response depend on vitamin A form, status, absorption, and host context; supplementation evidence is not a general dose-response claim for PM1.
The human study tested a pomegranate-juice matrix rather than isolated equivalence of every ellagitannin; final metabolite generation varies.
